id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point bus-independent core socket. Each OCP instance connects one master to one slave; a bus wrapper translates OCP to the on-chip interconnect so the core is isolated from the bus. Concurrency within a socket comes from threads, not from a shared bus.

supported_topologies.name: Master core <-> bus wrapper
supported_topologies.description: An IP core's OCP master socket connects point-to-point to a bus wrapper's OCP slave socket.

supported_topologies.name: Bus wrapper <-> slave core
supported_topologies.description: A bus wrapper's OCP master socket connects to a slave core's OCP slave socket.

supported_topologies.name: Peer-to-peer (two instances)
supported_topologies.description: Two entities communicate peer-to-peer with two OCP instances, one per direction.

supported_topologies.name: Multi-threaded socket
supported_topologies.description: A single OCP socket carrying concurrent independent threads (MThreadID/SThreadID).

master_slave_role_summary.description: The controlling entity; the only entity that presents commands (MCmd).
Responds to commands; asserts SCmdAccept and drives SResp/SData.
Presents an OCP slave socket to a master core and an OCP master socket to a slave core, bridging OCP to the on-chip interconnect.

fields.interconnect_role: OCP itself does not define an interconnect — it is a point-to-point socket. The on-chip bus behind the OCP wrapper provides address decoding, arbitration between masters, and routing; the wrapper translates between OCP phases and the bus protocol, so an OCP-wrapped core can be reused on any bus that provides an OCP wrapper.

ordering_guarantees.intra_thread: In order within a thread unless tags permit out-of-order responses.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: An OCP slave is address-mapped: the master drives MAddr (+ optional MAddrSpace) to select a location within the connected slave. OCP is point-to-point, so address decoding to multiple targets is the job of the bus behind the wrapper.

device_classification.slave: Memory / register peripheral responding to commands.
device_classification.bus_wrapper: Translates OCP to the on-chip interconnect.
device_classification.threaded_master: Issues concurrent transfers on multiple threads.
